status_reason: Material, quantity and location are known, so a provisional assessment is possible; reuse of the old calibration cannot be approved as the premise is wrong [P:S01-p15-1; S01-5-chemometrics].
answer: The old calibration cannot be assumed valid for the new API and excipient blend, and adding Raman does not keep it valid either. Test NIR diffuse reflection in the feed frame with a new calibration built on the new blend first. Then compare NIR alone against a fused NIR+Raman model on the same validation samples.

inline.headline: Test NIR diffuse reflection in the tablet press feed frame with a new calibration on the new blend, not reuse of the old model
inline.probe: NIR diffuse reflection probe for powder
inline.install: tablet press feed frame, as in the existing pilot
inline.test_against: NIR + Raman fused model (785 nm Raman probe) on the same validation samples
inline.not_final_because: The old calibration is not valid for the new blend; the pilot's spectral range and probe are not stated; NIR is quoted to 2500 nm but the silica fiber covers to 2400 nm; the Raman gain is only a hypothesis until tested.

problems.text: The old calibration cannot be assumed valid for the new API and excipient blend. NIR calibrations are chemometric models built, validated and then applied, so the old model must be re-tested and most likely replaced by a new calibration.

Adding Raman does not keep the old calibration valid. A combined NIR+Raman model is a new model built on fused data, needing its own calibration and validation on the new blend; whether fusion helps this blend is a hypothesis.
The pilot's spectral range and fiber are not stated. The silica Vis-NIR fiber covers 350-2400 nm, while NIR is quoted at 780-2500 nm, so confirm the range the pilot actually uses.
NIR and Raman must sample the same powder spot. Two separate probes used in turn cannot guarantee this, so a combined probe or synchronised acquisition is needed for any fused model.

methods.why: The pilot already exists; NIR penetrates several millimetres into dense solids and suits remote online fiber probes, but it needs a new chemometric calibration for the new blend.
The feed-frame study reported better API potency prediction with fused NIR+Raman than single-method models, in that study only; it must be tested on this blend.
Raman adds molecular backbone information, but its signals are weak and can be masked by fluorescence; it needs a 785 nm Raman fiber probe.
Mid-IR is limited to very thin layers, typically under 50 µm, and suits liquids and soft solids rather than a powder blend in a feed frame.

questions.q: What are the new API and excipients, and what is the target API concentration range and unit?
questions.why: Defines which spectral features matter and the calibration range.

questions.q: Which independent laboratory method gives the reference API values for the pilot, and how many reference samples exist?
questions.why: Reference values must come from independent laboratory analysis, not the instrument's own calibration.

questions.q: What spectral range and fiber does the NIR pilot use, and does it record above 2400 nm?
questions.why: The silica Vis-NIR fiber stops at 2400 nm.

questions.q: Is a 785 nm Raman fiber probe available, or is adding Raman only a suggestion at this stage?
questions.why: Raman needs its own probe and its own test on the new blend.

experiment.objective: Decide whether the old NIR calibration can be reused on the new blend, and whether fused NIR+Raman beats NIR alone on the same validation samples.
steps: Prepare laboratory samples of the new blend spanning the target API concentration range, with independent laboratory reference values.
Measure the samples with the existing NIR pilot probe and apply the old calibration as is to quantify the shift.
Build a new NIR chemometric calibration on the new blend and validate it on independent samples.
Record Raman (785 nm) on the same synchronised samples with a combined probe at the same spot, and build NIR-only and fused NIR+Raman models.
Compare the models on the same validation set and confirm the fiber covers the measured range before using spectra above 2400 nm.
references: De Man, A, et al. (2024). Evaluating the improvement of blend potency measurements in the feed frame of a rotary tablet press using combined NIR and Raman spectroscopy. Analytical Chemistry, 96(26), 10586-10593.
experiment.go_no_go: Criteria come from the client; none are stated in the enquiry.

pathway.key_features: Not yet known; to be identified from the new-blend spectra by multivariate analysis.
pathway.path_reason: The new calibration and key-feature selection on the new blend must be done in the lab trial first.

multispectral.why: Complementary information: NIR detects hydrogen bonds and polar groups, while Raman gives the molecular backbone and non-polar groups.
multispectral.test: Build a NIR-only model and a fused NIR+Raman model on the same new-blend calibration and validation samples; the fused model must beat the best single method on that set to count.

assumptions: The new blend is a powder fed to the tablet press feed frame.
The existing pilot uses a NIR diffuse reflection probe.
Independent reference values exist or can be made for pilot and new-blend samples.
Raman is not yet installed at the site.
